text:
Dr Helen Wu
Rehabilitation Specialist
South Melbourne Rehabilitation services 
123 Emerald Street
South Melbourne 3205
20/1/2007
Dear Dr Wu,
RE: Mr Jack Wojovski
I am writing this letter to refer Mr Wojovski whose features are suggestive of low back injury.
Mr Wojovski is married with troubles with his wife and she denies his sickness. He has been a factory worker for 18 year. 
Mr Wojovski story started on 28/12/2006 by reporting a persistent low back pain after lifting a heavy object at his work. On examination by the factory nurse, she found L4-L5 tenderness in the paralumbar area and the range of movement was limited. She advised him to take 2 days rest with analgesia. Her diagnosis was muscle strain in the lower back. 5 days later, he presented with worse persistent pain and inability to drive or bend despite of taking regular medications. However, there was no change in his physical examination. His management plan was Naprosyn and physiotherapy.
On 17/1/2007, the pain was relieved after 4 sessions of physiotherapy, but examination showed pain on forward flexion and L4-L5 tenderness. For that, he was advised to return to light duties at his work.
3 days ago, the condition deteriorated after returning to work. Accordingly, X ray lumbar spine was ordered. Today, the patient was not able to perform light duties and physiotherapy was just causing temporary relief of pain.
In view of the above, I think the patient shoud not return to work. I would appreciate it if you provide an assessment and management of his condition. 
Yours sincerely,
Doctor
